decided.question: does a client principal calling the create route or the grant route get REQ-03-019's 404, or the 403 REQ-03-027 and REQ-03-032 name
decided.chose: REQ-03-019 is bounded by an enumeration — the requests list, a request they are the addressee of, that request's answer, decline and message routes, and the create and grant routes — and every other organization route answers 404; create and grant answer the stated 403s and are the whole of the exception
decided.rejected: the absolute form, '404, never 403, on every organization route this spec does not grant them', which would have refused both with 404 and failed TC-03-INT-14 and TC-03-INT-22
decided.why: rule 2 and rule 3 — the 404 discipline exists so the staff product is not enumerable, and neither exception names a resource the caller cannot already see: grant acts on a request they may read, and the create refusal is a sentence written for a contact rather than the one a viewer gets. Hiding grant behind 404 would hide a request the caller is entitled to read
decided.recordedAt: REQ-03-019's rule and its Decided in specs/requests/03-client-participants.md; the Security bullet in the contracts now states the same boundary and names both messages, and AC-3 now claims 404 for the members, projects and contacts routes, which is what TC-03-INT-13 observes

decided.question: is inviting an existing contact of client A to client B refused at the invite, or written and left to fail at accept
decided.chose: refused at the invite: REQ-03-013 now answers 409 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.alreadyLinked when the address holds a ClientMembership of another client of the organization, whatever that row's status, or an active one of the named client
decided.rejected: leaving the cross-client invite to be written and refused at accept with principalConflict — the manager is told the invitation was sent and the contact meets the refusal instead; and dropping the step from TC-03-INT-07, which would have deleted coverage rather than settling the rule
decided.why: rule 3 — the refusal that fails safe is the one at the door, since REQ-03-002 lets an account hold one client principal and a second client's invitation could never be accepted; extending it to a removed row at another client closes the same question for accept, where returning that row to active under a new client would rebind a row the old client's requests still resolve through
decided.recordedAt: REQ-03-013's rule and its Decided in specs/requests/03-client-participants.md; the paragraph under the contracts' state table, which scopes `state` to the named client and says the removed|invite row is that client's own row; validation rule 2, edge case 3, the alreadyLinked message text (now 'This person is already a contact of a client in this workspace', true of both refusals so neither says which client), the client-contact-invite-error-email row, AC-15, and TC-03-INT-07, which adds the removed-row step

decided.question: does an assigneeClientMembershipId naming a contact of another organization answer 400 assigneeInactive or 404
decided.chose: 404 with no message, identical to an id that names no row at all; only a removed contact of the caller's own organization is 400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.assigneeInactive
decided.rejected: one constraint covering both activeness and organization with one 400 message, which tells a caller that an id belongs to somebody, somewhere
decided.why: rule 3 — the answer that hides is the one that cannot be used to probe contact ids across organizations, and it matches the 404 the rest of this spec gives a row the caller may not see
decided.recordedAt: REQ-03-020's rule and its Decided in specs/requests/03-client-participants.md; validation rule 6 (organization and existence, 404, no message) split from rule 7 (active, assigneeInactive) in the contracts, with the ordering sentence beneath the table renumbered and stating that rule 6 answers before rule 7; TC-03-INT-32 asserts the cross-organization id and an unknown id are alike

decided.question: do the three contacts routes answer a caller without the capability 403 with a message, or 404
decided.chose: 404 with no message on all three — GET without view-clients, POST and DELETE without manage-clients
decided.rejected: 403 CLIENT_MESSAGES.forbidden and 403 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.inviteForbidden; the inviteForbidden row and the forbidden row are deleted from the Error Messages table, since no route in this spec answers them
decided.why: rule 1 and rule 3 — the client resource these routes hang off already answers that caller 404 deliberately, and a distinctive 403 on a route hanging off it lets a `user` enumerate client ids the sibling route hides
decided.recordedAt: REQ-03-008, renamed 'who may manage contacts', with its Decided in specs/requests/03-client-participants.md; the three route rows and the paragraph under the Routes table in the contracts; TC-03-INT-12, which now asserts 404 on all three and says why

decided.question: does a client principal asking for scope=all get 200 with their own rows or the 403 the route answers a member without view-all-requests

decided.question: does accepting an invitation insert a ClientMembership, or return the account's existing row to active

decided.question: does a request response carry the contact's email address, or is the PII claim narrowed to the contacts list
decided.chose: narrowed: the address is visible on the contacts list to holders of ViewClients and nowhere else, and no request response carries it — the assignee member names the contact and their client only
decided.rejected: adding an email member to the assignee shape and naming who receives it, which would put PII on every request read by a party and by every holder of ViewAllRequests for a need no requirement states
decided.why: rule 3 and rule 4 — the narrower claim matches the response shape this spec already states, and widening the shape later is cheaper than retracting an address already served
decided.recordedAt: the PII bullet of the contracts' Security section, and the Known Gaps row in specs/requests/03-client-participants.md, which now names view-clients and the contacts list
